transcript.text: Mr. President, thank you for seeing me. I will be direct with you. Your headaches and fatigue may be the result of the extraordinary strain of your office — that would not surprise any physician in the country. But some of the symptoms concern me. I cannot rule out a deeper constitutional weakness. I must insist on further examination over the coming weeks, and I strongly recommend you reduce your working hours. I cannot yet say whether this is merely exhaustion or something more.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You’ll be pleased to know that I have just received word that my oldest son Robert is safe. He was taken aboard the transport ship from Fortress Monroe.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: That is welcome news indeed, Mr. President. A father’s relief must be a powerful tonic. Still, I must urge you not to let that relief distract you from what I’ve said. Your own constitution requires as much care as the nation’s.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your concern, Dr. Bell. I appreciate your vigilance in ensuring the well-being of both the President and his family. However, I assure you that I am not letting my personal health concerns distract me from the responsibilities of my position. The well-being of the nation is my utmost priority. Thank you for reminding me of that. I will take your advice seriously and consider reducing my working hours accordingly. Rest assured, I will continue to serve the United States with utmost dedication and commitment. Thank you for your concern, Dr. Bell. I appreciate it.

I would like to examine you again next week, and perhaps speak with Mrs. Lincoln about ensuring you rest.
